## This week

1. What if my predictor contains categories?
3. Common tests as linear models   

# categorical predictors

## lines again..  


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**The general idea:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{outcome}} &= \color{blue}{\text{model}} +  \color{black}{\text{error}} \\
\end{align}
$$
**The linear model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{y} &= \color{blue}{\underset{\underset{\text{intercept}}{\uparrow}}{b_0} + \underset{\underset{\text{slope}}{\uparrow}}{b_1} \cdot x} + \color{black}{\epsilon}
\end{align}
$$

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| fig-height: 8
maked <- function(b0=0,b1=0,g=1,e){
  df <- tibble(
    x = runif(100,-2,10),
    y = rnorm(100,b0+b1*x,e)
  )
  df
}
gets <- function(d){
  fitw = lm(y~x,d)
  segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0:6, x2 = x1+1) |> 
    mutate(
      y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
      y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
      xlp = (x1+x2)/2,
      ylp = (y1+y2)/2
    )
  segsw
}
df <- tibble(
  g = 1:20,
  b0 = rnorm(20,40,5),
  b1 = rnorm(20,0,2),
  e = rexp(20,.1)+1
) |>
  mutate(
    dd = pmap(list(b0,b1,g,e),~maked(..1,..2,..3,..4)),
    ss = map(dd,~gets(.))
  )

p_anim <- unnest(df,dd) |>
  ggplot(aes(x,y))+
  geom_point(size=3,alpha=.4)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(data = unnest(df,ss) |> filter(x1==0),
             aes(x=0,y=y1),col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = unnest(df,ss), aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = unnest(df,ss), aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:10)+
  transition_states(g, transition_length = 2, state_length = 6)

animp <- animate(p_anim, nframes = 500,
        fps = 15, end_pause = 45, res=150,
        width = 1000, height = 700, 
        renderer = gifski_renderer())

anim_save("jk_sandbox/eglines.gif", animp)
```
![](jk_sandbox/eglines.gif)

## that example again..  


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%" style="font-size:.6em"}

**The idea:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{outcome}} &= \color{blue}{\text{model}} + \color{black}{\text{error}} \\
\quad \\
\color{red}{y} &= \color{blue}{\underset{\underset{\text{intercept}}{\uparrow}}{b_0} + \underset{\underset{\text{slope}}{\uparrow}}{b_1} \cdot x} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
\end{align}
$$

**Our model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{NightsDisrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon} \\
\end{align}
$$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Our estimated model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{58 - 1.5 \cdot \text{NightsDisrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
\end{align}
$$
:::

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

:::{.r-stack}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(65683728)
sleepdf <- tibble(
  n_disrupted = rep(0:7,e=10),
  psolve = (58 - 1.5 * n_disrupted) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(80,0,7) ~ rep(0:7,e=10)))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)


fitw = lm(psolve~n_disrupted,sleepdf)

segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0:6, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    xlp = (x1+x2)/2,
    ylp = (y1+y2)/2
  )
sleepdf |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_disrupted,y=psolve))+
  geom_point(size=5,col="tomato1",alpha=.5)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:7)
```

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
sleepdf |>

  stat_smooth(method=lm,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
```

## that example again.. (2)

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Design:**  
People have 0, 1, 2, .... nights of sleep disruption.  

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Data:**  
```{r}
head(sleepdf)
```
:::
::::

**Model:**  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{NightsDisrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}

**Predictions:**  

$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 0} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 1} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 2} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 3} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
...

:::

## example 2

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(65683728)
xbin = sample(c("Good","Bad"),60,T,prob=c(.6,.4))
eg2sleep <- tibble(
  sleep_quality = xbin,
  psolve = (50 + 7.5 * (sleep_quality=="Good")) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(60,0,7) ~ xbin))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)

```

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Design:**  
People have "good" or "bad" sleep

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
**Data:**  
```{r}
head(eg2sleep)
```

:::
::::


**Model:**  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{SleepQuality}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}

**Predictions:**  

$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{'Bad'}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{'Good'}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  

:::

## doing maths with words  

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
head(eg2sleep)
```

- We can't multiply a number by a word.<br>$\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{'Bad'}}$<br>$\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{'Good'}}$<br>don't make sense 
    
:::
:::{.column width="50%" .fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: false
eg2sleep |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = (sleep_quality=="Good")*1, .after=sleep_quality
  ) |> head()
```

- But we can represent categories as binary 0/1 variables<br>$\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 0}$<br>$\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 1}$<br>using the binary variable makes the maths work

:::
:::: 


## expressing categories as numbers

With just two levels, we just map 0s and 1s to the two categories:  

```{r}
eg2sleep |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Good", 1, 0)
  )
```

## with 3+, we need more
#### (this doesn't come up again until DAPR2) 

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(3588)
xbin = sample(c("Good","Average","Bad"),60,T,prob=c(.2,.6,.2))
eg3sleep <- tibble(
  sleep_quality = xbin,
  psolve = (50 + 7.5 * (sleep_quality=="Good")) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(60,0,7) ~ xbin))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)

```

```{r}
eg3sleep |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Good", 1, 0),
    isBad = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Bad",1,0)
  )
```


## lm() does it for us!  

- variables in R can be:  
    - numeric
    - factor
    - character
    
- when a predictor is either character or factor, `lm()` will do this all for us.  


## lm() does it for us! - example 2


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
head(eg2sleep)
```
:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ 1 + sleep_quality, 
                    data = eg2sleep)

sleepqual_mod
```
:::
::::

:::dapr1callout
- the category named in the coefficients is coded as 1.  
- the category not mentioned is coded as 0.  
:::

## what are $b_0$ and $b_1$?  

**The Model:**  
$$
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot (\underbrace{\text{SleepQuality="Good"}}_{\text{1 if 'Good'}\\\text{0 otherwise}})} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

- for people with "Bad" sleep quality:  

$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 0} \\
 &= \color{blue}{b_0} \\
\end{align}
$$  

- for people with "Good" sleep quality:  

$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 1} \\
 &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 }
\end{align}
$$  


## what are $b_0$ and $b_1$?  

**The Model:**  
$$
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Good")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

```{r}

  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_quality, y=psolve))+
  # jitter adds a little noise to the data, so that points don't overlap
  # height and width control how much noise 
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```

## changing reference category?  

Do we want:  
<br>
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Good")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
  
  <br>
or  
  <br>
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Bad")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

## R defaults to alphabetical

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="65%"}

```{r}
#| eval: false
summary(sleepqual_mod)
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
.pp(summary(sleepqual_mod),l = list(c(1:14),0,0,0,0))
```

:::
:::{.column style="width:35%;font-size:.7em;color:#cc3363"}

<br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br>

- "Good" is mentioned here to indicate moving from the reference category to "Good"  
- the intercept (the reference category) must therefore be "Bad" because it's not mentioned in the slope  


:::

## factors give us control

```{r}
#| eval: false
eg2sleep <- eg2sleep |>
  mutate(
                                                # note the ordering
    sleep_quality = factor(sleep_quality, levels = c("Good", "Bad"))
    
  )

sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ 1 + sleep_quality, data = eg2sleep)
sleepqual_mod
```

:::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: false
eg2sleep <- eg2sleep |>
  mutate(
    sleep_quality = factor(sleep_quality, 
                           levels = c("Good", "Bad"))
  )

sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, data = eg2sleep)
sleepqual_mod
```
:::

## Write up

> We fit a simple linear regression model to estimate whether the quality of sleep ("Bad" vs "Good", treatment coded with "Good" as the reference level) would predict scores on a problem solving task. 
On average, people reporting "Good" sleep scored 50 on the problem solving task ($b=57.50, SE = 1.14, t(58) = 50.39, p<.001$). Compared to those who reported "Good" sleep, those who reported "Bad" sleep scored on average 7.5 points lower ($b = -7.50, SE = 1.88, t(58)=-3.98, p<.001$), with a 95% confidence interval of [-11.27, -3.73].


# common tests as linear model


## lm() with continuous predictor

$$
\color{red}{\text{Y}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{X}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

- $\color{blue}{b_0}$ = mean Y when X=0
- $\color{blue}{b_1}$ = change in mean Y from X=x to X=x+1

## lm() with binary predictor 

$$
\color{red}{\text{Y}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(X="categoryB")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

- $\color{blue}{b_0}$ = mean Y when X="categoryA"
- $\color{blue}{b_1}$ = change in mean Y from X="categoryA" to X="categoryB"

## spot the difference in means... (1) 

__t-test__  
```{r}
t.test(
  eg2sleep$psolve ~ eg2sleep$sleep_quality,
  var.equal = TRUE
)
```

## spot the difference in means... (2)  

__linear model__  
```{r}
sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ 1 + sleep_quality, 
                    data = eg2sleep)

summary(sleepqual_mod)
```


## back to correlations

- we started whole discussion of linear models with scatterplots and correlations.  

- correlation is a standardised metric for characterising the linear association

- "how many SDs does Y increase by, when X increases by 1 SD?"

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
- the shape of the distribution doesn't change. 
- just the numbers
:::

## coefficients change. model doesn't. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
sleepdf <- sleepdf |> mutate(id = row_number())
fitw = lm(psolve~n_disrupted,sleepdf)
segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    ll = as.character(round(coef(fitw)[2],2))
  )
fitw2 = lm(scale(psolve)~scale(n_disrupted),sleepdf)
segsw2 <- tibble(x1 = 0, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw2))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw2))[1]),
    ll = as.character(round(coef(fitw2)[2],2))
  )
dff <- bind_rows(
  sleepdf, 
  sleepdf |> mutate(n_disrupted = scale(n_disrupted)[,1],
                    psolve = scale(psolve)[,1]),
  .id = "frame"
)
segsw <- segsw |> mutate(seg_id = row_number())
segsw2 <- segsw2 |> mutate(seg_id = row_number())
sdf <- bind_rows(
  segsw, 
  segsw2,
  .id = "frame"
)


p_anim <- dff |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_disrupted,y=psolve))+
  geom_point( aes(group = id),size=5,col="tomato1",alpha=.5)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(data = sdf |> filter(x1==0),
             aes(x=0,y=y1),col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = sdf, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1,group=seg_id),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = sdf, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2,group=seg_id),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  geom_label(data = sdf, 
             aes(x = 1.1,y=(y1+(y2-y1)/2), label=ll),hjust=0) + 
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  labs(
    x = "{ifelse(closest_state == 1, 'n_disrupted',
            'Z(n_disrupted)')}",
    y = "{ifelse(closest_state == 1, 'psolve',
            'Z(psolve)')}"
  )+
  transition_states(frame, transition_length = 2, state_length = 6) +
  view_follow(fixed_x = FALSE, fixed_y = FALSE)

animp <- animate(p_anim, nframes = 150,
        fps = 15, end_pause = 15, res=150,
        width = 1000, height = 700, 
        renderer = gifski_renderer())

anim_save("jk_sandbox/line_z.gif", animp)
```

## spot the covariance... (1)

__cor.test__  
```{r}
cor.test(sleepdf$psolve, sleepdf$n_disrupted)
```

## spot the covariance... (2)

__linear model__  
```{r}
sleep_mdl <- lm(psolve ~ 1 + n_disrupted,
                data = sleepdf)

summary(sleep_mdl)
```

## spot the covariance... (3)

__linear model with Z-scored variables__  
```{r}
#| eval: false
sleepdf <- sleepdf |>
  mutate(
    Zpsolve = (psolve - mean(psolve)) / sd(psolve),
    Zn_disrupted = (n_disrupted - mean(n_disrupted)) / sd(n_disrupted)
  )

sleep_mdlZ <- lm(Zpsolve ~ 1 + Zn_disrupted,
                data = sleepdf)

summary(sleep_mdlZ)
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
sleepdf <- sleepdf |>
  mutate(
    Zpsolve = (psolve - mean(psolve)) / sd(psolve),
    Zn_disrupted = (n_disrupted - mean(n_disrupted)) / sd(n_disrupted)
  )
sleep_mdlZ <- lm(Zpsolve ~ 1 + Zn_disrupted,
                data = sleepdf)
ss <- summary(sleep_mdlZ)
ss$coefficients[,1] <- round(ss$coefficients[,1],3)
ss
```
